# Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines and file refactor work items

## Problem statement

The refactor skill detects `god_class` and `long_method` via LLM judgement, but
has **no deterministic file-size signal**. Files therefore grow far past a
readable size unnoticed: the ContextHub repo sweep that produced
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts, 8,205 lines) found **15 production
files over 1,000 lines** — `worklist.ts` 7,792, `database.ts` 3,684,
`index.ts` 2,784 and eleven more — none of which the skill had ever flagged.

File length is a cheap, objective, language-independent maintainability proxy
and belongs in the skill's default rule set, not in ad-hoc producer sweeps.

## Users

- **Producers/agents running `/skill:refactor`** want oversized files surfaced
  automatically instead of discovered by manual `wc -l` sweeps.
- **Maintainers** want a consistent 1,000-line ceiling applied across every
  project without re-deriving the rule each time.
- **Reviewers** want refactor work items to exist before a file becomes
  unmaintainable, with an explicit "is refactoring appropriate?" judgement
  recorded.

User stories:

- As a producer running a full-project refactor scan, I want every file over
  1,000 lines listed so that I can decide which to decompose.
- As an agent, I want a work item filed automatically when a large file
  genuinely warrants decomposition, so that the finding is not lost.

## Goal

Add a deterministic **file-length** smell to the refactor skill: any source file
over 1,000 lines is flagged, evaluated by the existing LLM smell-detection pass
for whether refactoring is appropriate, and — when appropriate — a Worklog work
item is created through the existing `workitem_creation` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic pre-LLM scan flags every tracked source file whose line
   count exceeds a configurable threshold (default 1,000), reporting
   path, line count and excess.
2. The threshold is configurable via `.refactor.json` (e.g.
   `"file_length": {"enabled": true, "threshold": 1000}`) and disabled when set
   to `0`/`false`; the default applies with no config present.
3. Over-threshold files are passed to the LLM evaluation step, which decides
   whether decomposition is appropriate and records a one-line rationale;
   files judged not to warrant decomposition are reported but create no work
   item.
4. For appropriate files, exactly one Worklog work item is created (tags
   `Refactor`), idempotently — re-running the scan does not create a duplicate
   (existing REFACTOR-comment and `wl list --tags Refactor` dedup guards apply).
5. Generated test files/vendored/generated paths are excluded from the
   threshold check, and the exclusion list is configurable.
6. Unit tests cover: over/under threshold, config override/disable, LLM
   "not appropriate" suppression, dedup on re-run, and exclusion patterns.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`skill/refactor/SKILL.md` smell-type table and `.refactor.json` example).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing rule/config plumbing (`smell_detection.DEFAULT_RULES`,
  `scripts/config.py`, `workitem_creation.create_smell_work_item`) rather than
  adding a parallel mechanism.
- Deterministic and offline: the line-count scan must work with the LLM
  disabled (report-only) and must not require a network call.
- No behavioural change to existing smell types or their severities.

## Desired change

- New `file_length` rule + deterministic detector feeding the existing smell
  pipeline; severity `medium` by default (high above ~2× threshold).
- LLM prompt extension: for `file_length` findings, answer "does this file have
  multiple separable concerns that warrant decomposition?" with a rationale.
- Work-item title format consistent with existing generated titles, e.g.
  `Refactor: decompose <path> god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines)`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` — add `file_length` to `DEFAULT_RULES`
  smell types and a deterministic line-count detector.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py` — default config entry and threshold.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — wire the detector into the scan and
  pass findings to the LLM evaluation.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — ensure `file_length` titles/descriptions
  and dedup behave correctly.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the new smell type, config key and
  exclusion defaults.
- `skill/refactor/tests/` — unit tests for AC1–AC6.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (ContextHub) — the downtime-worker.ts god-class item whose
  manual sweep exposed the gap: 15 production files over 1,000 lines, prompting
  the producer directive that every such file be evaluated and, if appropriate,
  given a refactor work item.
- ContextHub follow-up refactor items created from that sweep (worklist.ts,
  database.ts, persistent-store.ts ×2, index.ts, fetcher.ts,
  dispatcher-anchor.ts, downtime-log.ts, sync.ts, github.ts, github-sync.ts,
  interview.ts, doctor.ts, init.ts).

## Assumptions

- 1,000 lines is the default ceiling; projects may override it per repo.
- "Evaluated for refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"
  is implemented as an LLM judgement gate, not an unconditional filing, so the
  scan does not flood backlogs with items for unavoidably large generated or
  data-heavy modules.
- Test files are in scope for the check by default (large test suites also
  warrant decomposition); generated/vendored paths are excluded.
data.title: Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate refactor need, and file work items

> **Migrated from the `llm` worklog:** this item was originally filed there as `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` (deleted after migration on 2026-10-20). The `llm` repo remains the sweep target for its markers listed below; all skill-code changes live here in `SorraAgents`.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs here (this `SA-` item) and owns the `llm` marker sweep alongside the `SorraAgents` sweep; Q1 is resolved by this migration.
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — ~~implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?~~ **RESOLVED** by migration: this `SA-` item hosts the skill change; the `llm` marker list below stays the sweep target.
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`? (moot — item migrated to `SorraAgents` as `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`)" — **OPEN QUESTION**. # Add an `--instructions` switch to the speak CLI for tone/style control

## Problem statement

The local CosyVoice 3 TTS server supports an optional `instructions` field on
`POST /v1/audio/speech` that routes to `inference_instruct2`, enabling
natural-language delivery control (excited, calm, warm, slow, whisper, etc.)
while preserving the cloned voice's timbre. That capability is delivered in
the `tts` project as **TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X** (completed, merged to
`origin/dev`).

The `speak` CLI cannot use it:

- `skill/speak/scripts/speak.sh` accepts only `--stream`, `--voice` and
  `--help`; the JSON payload hardcodes `model`, `input` and `voice`.
- `speak.py` is a pure pass-through timing wrapper, so it inherits the gap.
- Consequently pi agents and the operator cannot ask for a different delivery
  for a given voice (e.g. an excited tone on the `sorra` clone).

Discovered while verifying the `sorra` voice and the tone-instruction API
(TTS-0MVDZIS0O0060SRF, `tts` project).

## Users

- **Operator** — wants `speak.sh --instructions "excited and energetic" ...`.
- **pi agents / `/skill:speak`** — pass a tone instruction per invocation.
- **Maintainers** — keep default behaviour byte-identical; the field must be
  additive.

### User stories

- As the **operator**, I want to add a delivery instruction to a speak call so
  the same cloned voice can sound excited, calm, warm, etc.
- As an **existing caller**, I want calls that omit the instruction to behave
  exactly as today (no `instructions` key in the payload).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New CLI switch**: `speak.sh --instructions <text>` adds
   `"instructions": "<text>"` to the `/v1/audio/speech` JSON payload in both
   save-to-file and `--stream` modes. Verification: unit test with the mock
   curl payload capture asserts the exact value.
2. **Omitted → unchanged**: when `--instructions` is not supplied (and
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS` unset), the payload contains **no** `instructions` key
   and every existing test passes unchanged. Verification: payload-capture
   test asserts key absence; existing suite green.
3. **Safe JSON encoding**: instruction text containing quotes, backslashes or
   newlines round-trips through the payload exactly as supplied (reuse the
   existing `python3 -c 'json.dumps'` approach). Verification: payload-capture
   test parses the JSON and compares strings.
4. **Blank treated as omitted**: `--instructions ""` or whitespace-only is
   ignored (no key sent), never sent as an empty string. Verification: test.
5. **Length guard**: instructions longer than 500 characters fail fast with a
   clear error and non-zero exit **before** any network call (the server
   enforces the same limit with HTTP 400). Verification: test asserts curl was
   not invoked.
6. **Precedence + env default**: explicit `--instructions` wins over
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS`, which acts as the default when the flag is absent —
   mirroring the existing `--voice`/`TTS_VOICE` design. Verification: tests for
   the precedence and env-only paths.
7. **Consistent argument parsing**: `--instructions=<text>` is rejected with
   the same actionable hint already used for `--voice=<name>`; a bare
   `--instructions` with a missing or next-option value errors out with usage.
   Verification: tests for both error paths.
8. **Help + docs**: `speak.sh --help` lists the new option and the
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS` env var; `skill/speak/SKILL.md` documents usage with a
   tone example and notes the server-side dependency (endpoints without the
   extension ignore or reject the field). Verification: help-output test and
   doc-content test (mirroring the existing `test_skill_doc_exists`).
9. **No regressions**: full SorraAgents test suite passes; the wrapper
   `speak.py` continues to forward arguments untouched (no code change
   expected) and its tests pass.

## Constraints

- **Canonical location**: the skill is versioned at `skill/speak/` in this
  repository (`~/.pi/agent/skills/speak` is a symlink). Edit here.
- **Server dependency**: `instructions` is a non-standard extension. The
  server must run a build that includes TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X; older servers
  silently ignore the unknown field, so the CLI cannot verify that the
  instruction was applied. Document this.
- **No API changes to `speak.py`**: it must remain a pass-through.
- **Backwards compatibility**: default payload shape and behaviour are
  unchanged when no instruction is supplied.
- **Transport**: plain `curl` with a JSON body; no new runtime dependencies.

## Key Files

- `skill/speak/scripts/speak.sh` — add option parsing + payload field.
- `skill/speak/SKILL.md` — document the switch, env var and dependency.
- `tests/test_speak.py` — payload-capture tests (the mock curl already records
  the `-d` body to `payload.json`).

## Related work

- **TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X** (`tts` project) — server-side `instructions` field
  routed to `inference_instruct2`; completed and merged to `origin/dev`.
  This item consumes that contract.
- **TTS-0MVDZIS0O0060SRF** (`tts` project) — `sorra` voice clone; discovered
  from this verification session.
- Cross-project dependency edges cannot be recorded in this Worklog store;
  recorded here instead.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Version skew (medium)**: an older TTS server ignores `instructions`
  silently; the CLI produces neutral audio with no error. Mitigation: document
  the requirement and the expected HTTP behaviour.
- **Prompt-quality variance (low)**: instruction adherence and speaker
  similarity vary by phrasing (the server item recorded a 0.75–0.85 similarity
  range vs 0.857 neutral). Mitigation: document example phrasings, not
  promises.
- **Assumption**: the OpenAI-compatible field name is `instructions` (as
  implemented in TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X) and its 500-character limit is stable.
- **Assumption**: `--voice` parsing semantics are the template for the new
  switch (space-separated only; `=` form rejected with a hint).

## Problem

When an agent runs `audit_runner.py issue <id>` in the foreground (e.g. via a
tool command with a timeout), the runner can be killed mid-audit — for example
when the agent's tool timeout (600 s) fires during Phase 1 or Phase 2 LLM calls
which each have 600–1800 s budgets.

When the runner is killed:

1. **The work item is left in `in_progress`** — the runner's abort-recovery
   `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handlers restore the pre-audit state only if the Python
   process can run them. A hard kill (SIGKILL, tool timeout) skips them, leaving
   the item stranded in `in_progress`.
2. **The abort-state file** (`.audit_state_<id>.json`) persists on disk. On
   relaunch, if you do not restore the pre-audit state first, the runner captures
   `in_progress` as the "original" state and the relaunch becomes a no-op
   (or worse: overwrites the stored audit with stale content).
3. **The phase checkpoint** (`.worklog/audit-checkpoints/<id>.checkpoint.json`)
   survives the kill and the relaunch **will resume** from the furthest completed
   phase — so the work is not lost, but the manual state fix is required.

## Correct procedure

Always launch audits as a detached background task, then watch with the shared
wait script:

```bash
# 1. Launch detached
mkdir -p ~/.audit_debug/<project>/
LOG=~/.audit_debug/<project>/<id>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
nohup python3 \
  $(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id> \
  --worklog-dir <repo>/.worklog \
  > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!

# 2. Watch with the wait script (follows background-job etiquette)
python3 \
  $(skill_path shared)/wait_for_job.py \
  --pid $PID \
  --log "$LOG" \
  --pattern 'Phase 2|Skipping Phase 2|Per-call timing|Ready to close|Final verdict|ERROR|Traceback|partial' \
  --timeout 840 \
  --message "Waiting for audit of <id>"
```

The wait script prints periodic progress and exits when the audit completes or
times out. After it returns, inspect the log:

```bash
# Check if it succeeded
grep "Ready to close:" "$LOG"
# Or tail the end
tail -20 "$LOG"
```

## Recovery if already killed

If you discover an audit runner still running (e.g. `ps aux | grep
audit_runner`), or you killed one in the foreground and the item is stuck in
`in_progress`:

```bash
# 1. Restore pre-audit state (read from the abort-state file or known original)
wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review --assignee "" --json

# 2. Remove the abort-state file
rm -f .worklog/.audit_state_<id>.json /tmp/.audit_state_<id>.json

# 3. Relaunch detached (as above). The checkpoint will resume from the furthest
#    completed phase — no wasted work.
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit skill's `Monitored Run Execution` section (SKILL.md) includes a
   **mandatory launch procedure** that explicitly states: "ALWAYS launch
   detached; NEVER run `audit_runner.py issue` in the foreground."
2. A short **recovery procedure** is documented (as above) for the case where
   the agent is already mid-audit and must restore state before relaunching.
3. The `Monitored Run Execution` summary is cross-linked or mirrors the
   background-job etiquette (`skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md`) so
   agents see the same guidance in both places.

## Key files

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — audit skill documentation (Monitored Run Execution section)
- `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` — shared background-job etiquette
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the runner (has abort-recovery handlers)
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — the wait script for monitoring

## Notes

- The runner **does** have abort-recovery handlers (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`) and
  writes an abort-state file, so the item is never permanently stuck — but the
  manual restore step is required before relaunch.
- Phase checkpoints mean work is never lost; the relaunch is fast (resumes from
  the last completed phase).
- This is a documentation-only change; no code changes needed.
data.title: Audit skill: always launch as detached background task, never foreground

# Add a session-time-analysis skill ("where does Pi time go") and weave it into agent-log-review

## Summary
On 2026-10-21 an ad-hoc analysis of all 25 active Pi sessions in AI_Hell (00:52 to 18:54 local) answered the
operator question "where is the time going?": about 8.7 h of ~11.8 h active wall-clock was spent blocked in
wait_for_job.py (37 waits, avg ~15 min); one hung evaluate.mjs command burned 2.8 h; test runs ~1.4 h;
>96% of ~123 M tokens were cache reads. The analysis used throwaway scripts in /tmp/pi_time/
(analyse.py, deep.py, final.py, theme.py, content.py) which will not survive a reboot.

This item formalises that methodology into a maintained skill in skill/ (installed globally via
scripts/install_pi.sh) and integrates it with the existing agent-log-review skill so "where the time went"
becomes a standard, deterministic section of agent-log-review reports. It should improve on the ad-hoc
analysis where possible (see Design points) rather than merely port it.

## User stories
- As an operator I want to run one command per project and get a deterministic time-attribution report
  (window, session count by kind, active vs blocked vs LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) so I can see
  where agent-hours go without writing throwaway scripts.
- As an operator I want the same skill to flag waste (long blocked waits, hung commands, error-heavy tools,
  retry loops) so I can act on the biggest time sinks.
- As a maintainer of agent-log-review I want the v3 JSONL session parser and signal extractors shared and
  reused so time analysis is consistent with pattern analysis, and reports gain a "Where the time went"
  section.

## Design points (improvements over the throwaway scripts)
- Metrics: per-session AND union (de-duplicated across concurrent sessions) figures for wall, active
  (LLM+tool), LLM durationMs, tool and model split; token economics (input/output/cacheRead, cache-hit %);
  tool-error rates; timezone-correct day windowing; sessions spanning midnight; malformed lines degrade.
- Blocking classification by command intent (wait_for_job waits, test runs, git/build, implement.py
  orchestration, wl, inspection). The 2026-10-21 classifier mis-bucketed a 2.8 h hung node run under "git"
  because the command string contained a git subcommand: primary-binary/first-token attribution plus
  duration-outlier flagging is required, and the report must surface the top-N longest commands.
- Hung-command detection: per-command duration outliers vs typical duration for that command family.
- Report: deterministic Markdown (default) and JSON (--json), --output-file, --cwd/--session-root,
  --max-sessions; optional --parent-id worklog integration mirroring agent-log-review's idempotent comments.
- Integration with agent-log-review: factor the session parser + signal extraction into shared modules
  consumed by both skills; extend agent-log-review's distilled signals with time/blocking/waste features;
  add the time-attribution section to its report and a time-waste category to its classification prompt,
  WITHOUT weakening its privacy guarantees (raw logs never sent to a model; secrets redacted).

## Acceptance criteria
1. A new skill under skill/ with SKILL.md plus scripts/ and tests/ following agent-log-review's structure;
   deterministic CLI with every flag documented in --help.
2. Report covers: window, session count by kind (e.g. audit vs interactive), union active wall time,
   LLM vs tool split, per-tool time/calls/errors, per-model time, token & cache economics, blocking
   classification totals, and top-10 longest bash commands with hang flagging.
3. Union (de-duplicated) and naive-sum figures are both reported and explained: on 2026-10-21 sum-LLM was
   10.0 h vs union 6.5 h; the report must make the double-counting distinction explicit.
4. agent-log-review reports gain the time-attribution section sourced from shared extractors, and its
   classification prompt receives time/waste signals; privacy/redaction guarantees preserved.
5. Automated tests cover: parser/metrics (malformed lines, midnight-spanning sessions, millisecond vs ISO
   timestamps, empty dir, missing usage degrade, no crash) and a golden fixture from the 2026-10-21 AI_Hell
   sessions asserting the headline figures (~8.7 h blocked-wait of ~11.8 h active). Tests run under the
   repo's test policy (test skill).
6. SKILL.md documents usage, metric definitions, limitations (provider durationMs may skew under slot
   contention; host-load correlation initially out of scope) and the integration contract with
   agent-log-review.

## Context and references
- Throwaway working scripts (do not depend on them long-term): /tmp/pi_time/{analyse,deep,final,theme,content}.py
- Session logs: ~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl (v3 format)
- Existing skill to integrate with: skill/agent-log-review (SKILL.md, scripts/agent_log_review.py, tests/) — epic SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC
- Repo conventions: skills live in skill/ with scripts/ and tests/; global install via scripts/install_pi.sh;
  changes affect every project, so they must be tracked here, built, tested, and pushed to dev before re-install;
  UK English; follow existing skill conventions.
- Sample dataset: AI_Hell sessions 2026-10-21 (union active 11.76 h; blocked-wait 8.72 h union / 9.54 h sum
  across 37 waits; hung tune run 2.78 h; test runs ~1.4 h; tokens in 4.3 M / out 0.31 M / cacheRead 118 M;
  plan 7.96 h vs code 2.06 h).
- Use the effort-and-risk skill during planning.

# Intake Brief (v2) — Echo implement.py's live progress into the Pi client

## Problem statement

When an agent runs `implement.py finish` as a background job and waits on it
with `wait_for_job.py`, the operator in the Pi TUI sees **no feedback about
what the job is doing** for the entire wait — only the final elapsed marker
afterwards. Two distinct defects combine to cause this:

1. **`implement.py` is silently dark during the phases that take the time.**
   `run_build` (npm run build), `run_tests` (the full changed-scope suite),
   and `git_push_to_dev` all run their subprocesses fully captured
   (`capture_output=True` / `Popen(..., stdout=PIPE).communicate()`), so
   nothing is written to the job log while build/tests/push are actually
   running. A 2m36s (or 40-minute) wait sees only a few `LOG.info` phase
   lines — there is nothing for any watcher (TUI or log) to show.
2. **The waiter's relay loses bursty output.** Even when the job *does* write
   output, `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` keeps only the last `--tail-lines`
   (default 10) lines of each poll window and silently drops the earlier
   lines; a poll window that catches 200 build lines shows only 10.
3. **Operators accidentally defeat the streaming that does exist.** Piping the
   wait through `tail -N`/`grep`/`head` buffers everything until EOF — the Pi
   TUI then receives *zero* partial output (it CAN stream: the bash tool emits
   `tool_execution_update` with partial results, verified in
   `pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/bash.js`).

## Users

- **Operators / producers** watching an interactive `pi` TUI while the agent
  waits on `implement.py finish` (also audit, ship, epics).
  - *User story:* "As an operator watching a 20-minute `finish`, I want to see
    what the build, tests, and push are printing *as they run*, so I can tell
    whether the job is progressing or silently hung."
- **Agents** running the wait — they need a low-context-cost way to keep the
  waiter's own chattiness bounded without disabling the job-output stream.

## Root cause (verified in source)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: every subprocess is captured —
  `run_cmd(capture=…)` (line ~366), `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)`
  (~672, ~1835, ~4805, ~5431) and `Popen(…).communicate()` for the push
  (~1506–1515). The `logging.basicConfig` (line ~6063) writes `LOG.info`
  phase lines to stderr (→ the job log via `2>&1`), so the log holds phase
  headers but no live payload.
- `skill/test_cache.py::run_cached` → `_default_runner` (line ~405):
  `subprocess.run(shlex.split(command), …)` with stdout/stderr captured.
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py::JobOutputTail.new_lines`: returns
  `lines[-self.tail_lines:]` — silent drop of anything above the cap.
- Pi's bash tool *does* stream partial output (verified in the installed pi
  bundle); nothing in the tool chain prevents a live echo once the job
  actually emits output and the wait is not piped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **implement.py streams live phase output.** Build, test, and push steps
   relay their subprocess output to implement.py's own stdout/stderr **as it
   is produced** (a tee-style runner: read child stdout incrementally, forward
   each line with flush, still capture the full text for the step report and
   the `--json` contract). Phase transitions are printed as flush banners
   (e.g. `→ Running build (npm run build)…`, `→ Running tests (changed
   scope)…`, `→ Pushing to dev…`), so the log has a continuous, honest
   heartbeat even when a child is quiet.
2. **Test steps stream through the cache runner.** The streamed output path is
   wired through `test_cache.run_cached`'s runner seam (implement.py's
   changed-scope gate uses it), so the finish gate's *real* suite output is
   what appears live — not just the wrapper's banners.
3. **No silent drops in the waiter relay.** `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` no
   longer silently discards lines above `--tail-lines`; it either emits **all**
   new lines or emits an explicit omission marker
   (`… N lines omitted; raise --tail-lines or poll faster`). Default
   behaviour must be lossless for typical poll windows.
4. **Never pipe the waiter.** `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` and
   the `wait_for_job.py` module docstring state explicitly that the waiter's
   output must not be piped through `tail`/`head`/`grep` (it buffers and kills
   live UI streaming); the supported alternatives for bounding context
   (`--tail-lines`, `--interval`) are documented.
5. **Skills carry the rule.** The `implement` skill's `wait_for_job.py`
   example shows the rule at the point of use; remaining skills
   (`audit`/`ship`/`test`/`plan`) reference it.
6. **Behavioural tests.** Unit tests cover: streaming runner forwards child
   lines with flush and still captures; omission marker appears on overflow;
   a single liveness line per wait poll (no duplicate `progress:`+`heartbeat:`
   pair); existing timeout/completion/interrupt and `--json` behaviour
   unchanged.
7. **Docs-lint test.** A test asserts no skill doc shows a recommended
   `wait_for_job.py` invocation piped through `tail`/`grep`/`head`, and that
   the anti-pattern rule exists in the shared doc.
8. **Docs updated.** All related documentation reflects the change (code
   comments, docstrings, shared etiquette doc, skill docs).
9. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility.** `wait_for_job.py` CLI surface and exit codes
  (0/1/2/130) unchanged; `--json` output shape machine-parseable.
- **implement.py CLI contract preserved.** Streamed output is additive
  (stdout/stderr); the `--json` finish report format must not change.
- **No buffering regressions.** Every emitted line flushes; the helper stays
  usable when stdout *is* a pipe (pi's bash tool always pipes stdout — that is
  fine; only an intermediate buffering command breaks streaming).
- **Driven children run `--no-extensions`.** Do not propose a pi extension or
  custom tool as the fix; the repair lives in `implement.py`, `wait_for_job.py`,
  and the skill/doc guidance.
- **Silent degradation preserved** when `HERDR_*` env vars are absent.
- **No ad-hoc full-suite test runs during implementation** (slot contention /
  test-execution policy); changed-scope gate only.

## Existing state

- `wait_for_job.py` already flushes each line, tails the job's log
  incrementally, reports herdr sidebar state and process vitals
  (SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK + SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA).
- `implement.py` logs phase headers but captures all subprocess output;
  nothing streams during build/tests/push.
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` gives the established
  docs-lint pattern.

## Desired change

A finish run whose build/test/push output is **visible line-by-line** in the
Pi TUI (streamed by implement.py → log → waiter → bash-tool partial updates),
with an enforcement layer (docs rule + lint test) so agents do not pipe the
waiter away.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — tee-style live runner for
  build/tests/push; flush phase banners; wire through `run_build`,
  `run_tests`/`run_cached`, `git_push_to_dev`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` test seam / `skill/test_cache.py`
  runner — streaming runner passed to `run_cached(runner=…)`.
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — lossless (or explicit-omission) tail;
  single liveness line per poll; anti-pattern docstring.
- `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` — "Never pipe the waiter"
  subsection.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (+ `audit`/`ship`/`test`/`plan`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`) — rule at the point of use.
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` — docs-lint assertion.
- New behavioural tests (streaming runner, tail omission, liveness line).

## Related work

- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — *User-visible progress feedback in the Pi agent
  interface during long-running waits (wait_for_job)* (completed) — delivered
  the waiter-side streaming (tail, vitals, notification). This item fixes the
  producer side (`implement.py` silence) and the relay's silent drops.
- **SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK** — helper contract preserved by AC6.
- **SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT** — *Roll out background-job etiquette* — file list
  extended by AC5/AC7.
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — *Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts* —
  wiring table: `implement.py` marked "not appropriate" for *waiting* on a
  background job (unchanged — this item makes implement.py a *producer* of
  streamable output, not a waiter).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (verified in pi source):** the interactive TUI updates its
  pending-tool box on `tool_execution_update`, so streamed output is genuinely
  visible. If a future pi release removes streaming, this item's guidance is
  harmless but the visible benefit disappears.
- **Risk — streaming stdout in implement.py could interleave with `--json`
  report output.** Mitigation: stream to stderr (matching the existing
  "timing goes to stderr" convention, SA-0MT319YGQ002E801) so `--json`
  stdout stays clean. Note: the job log captures both via `2>&1`.
- **Risk — performance.** Tee-streaming adds per-line reads; acceptable for
  build/test/push cadence; keep line-buffered reads, not byte-at-a-time.
- **Risk — test tooling divergence.** `run_tests` delegates to
  `test.scripts.run_tests` / `test_cache.run_cached`; the runner seam must be
  exercised without bypassing the cache or the slot guard.
- **Scope-creep:** a pi-extension `wait_job` tool that renders progress is
  deliberately out of scope (driven children run `--no-extensions`).
- **Enforcement is by docs-lint, not runtime**; a determined agent can still
  pipe. Acceptable, bounded risk.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the missing feedback because pi does not stream bash output, or
  because of how the command was invoked?
  — **Answer (Map):** The invocation (`… | tail -25`) breaks streaming, but it
  is not the whole story. Pi's bash tool emits partial output via
  `onUpdate` → `tool_execution_update` (`dist/core/tools/bash.js`), and
  `wait_for_job.py` flushes each line — so *any* job output would stream. The
  larger cause is that `implement.py` writes almost nothing during build/tests
  (all subprocess output captured).

- **Q:** (v1) So deduplicating the waiter's heartbeat lines and telling agents
  not to pipe would fix the complaint?
  — **Answer (operator correction):** No — that only relays implement.py's
  sparse phase headers. The build/test/push *output* never reaches the log at
  all. v2 re-scopes to make implement.py produce live, streamed output
  (AC1–AC2) plus fix the relay's silent drops (AC3) plus the never-pipe rule
  (AC4–AC5). Verified: all six subprocess sites in implement.py capture
  output; `run_cached`/`_default_runner` capture too.

- **Q:** Should the streamed output go to stdout or stderr?
  — **Answer (Map):** stderr, matching the existing "timing to stderr"
  convention (`_emit_timing`, SA-0MT319YGQ002E801) so `--json` stdout stays
  clean. The nohup invocation captures both (`> log 2>&1`), so the log and
  therefore the waiter/tail see it either way.

- **Q:** Is there any live feedback *today*, before this item lands?
  — **Answer (Map):** Yes, partial: (a) the waiter's own heartbeat lines
  (`progress:`/`heartbeat:` with `state=/cpu=/children=` vitals) stream if the
  wait is unpiped; (b) herdr sidebar `working`/`blocked` when
  `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`+`HERDR_PANE_ID` are exported; (c) `WAIT_NOTIFY=1` →
  `notify-send` on completion. None of these show what implement.py is doing —
  the new capability is a teed child-output stream.
data.title: Echo implement.py's live build/test/push output into the Pi client (stream, don't pipe)

# Commit hooks exec a hard-coded per-user path → `git worktree add` and `wl sync` fail

## Problem statement

The committed hooks `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
`.githooks/post-rewrite` unconditionally `exec` the absolute path
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. That path is
per-user and machine-specific, so on any host where it is absent (a different
username, a clean machine, CI) every checkout, merge and `git worktree add` in
this repository exits 127 — which in turn breaks `wl sync` (its
temporary-worktree merge) and `implement.py start`/`finish` worktree creation.
The repository already commits the real script as `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`,
but no wrapper references it.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
# The wrapper hard-codes an absolute path, so the failure is independent of
# $HOME. Simulate a host where that path does not exist by moving the central
# symlink aside for one command (restore it afterwards):
LINK=$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull
mv "$LINK" "$LINK.bak"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-repro HEAD
mv "$LINK.bak" "$LINK"
# → .githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
# → rc=127 (verified during intake)
```

On the current agent host the immediate trigger is masked because
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists as a symlink to
this repo's committed script (installed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so normal
runs here exit 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing"). The
defect is therefore latent on this host and reproduces on every host or clean
clone where that absolute path is absent.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs `implement.py start`/`finish`
  to create worktrees without a hook failure aborting the run.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.
  Story: *As a maintainer of the agent framework, I need a test that fails if a
  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **No hard-coded per-user path.** The three wrappers
      (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`) resolve the
      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try
      the repository-relative `<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then
      `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and when neither exists
      they print one clear line to stderr and exit 0 (never 127, never a silent
      failure).
- [ ] **Regression test proving `git worktree add` succeeds.** A hermetic test
      asserts (a) the committed wrappers contain no absolute `/home/<user>` or
      other machine-specific path; (b) in a temp repository built from the
      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed
      `$HOME` that has no `.config/pi`, and a stubbed `wl` on `PATH`,
      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no
      `exec: ... not found`, and reaches the repo-relative
      `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; and (c) the same setup with
      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).
- [ ] **`wl sync` completes its push step** in this repository on a host
      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hooks are POSIX `sh` executed by git; they must stay dependency-free (no
  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /
  `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve the existing bypass variables (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`,
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) and their documented semantics.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The three wrappers are 184-byte files with header
  `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` and a single
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"` line
  (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **is committed** (514 bytes; runs `wl sync`,
  honours `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, fail-open when `wl` is absent). Nothing
  in the repository invokes it: `rg worklog-post-pull` finds only the wrappers'
  hard-coded path, `scripts/install_pi.sh` (central install), one test file and
  the docs.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the central script as an executable symlink
  to the repo copy (`create_symlink`, idempotent, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  gated) and then emits a **warning only** when a project's committed wrapper
  does not reference that central path. The warning does not fix the wrapper.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (~lines 100–120) documents the delegation and
  carries a "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph describing
  exactly this defect as unresolved.
- Sibling repositories (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) ship
  self-contained `post-checkout`/`worklog-post-pull` hooks that (a) skip
  `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and (b) skip linked worktrees
  (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir`). The SorraAgents copy of
  `worklog-post-pull` lacks both guards. (`ContentCreator` is reported in the
  consolidated duplicate item to have the same self-contained pattern, but that
  checkout is not present on this host, so it was not verified directly.)
- Verified on this host: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-intake-check HEAD`
  now exits 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing") because
  the central symlink exists — the hard-coded path is what breaks elsewhere.
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` covers the *installer* and writes
  its own synthetic hooks; no test asserts the content or behaviour of this
  repository's committed wrappers.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` and `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
  cover the pre-push wiring only.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the three wrappers to resolve the post-pull script in this order:
   repository-relative (via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"`), then `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then a
   single-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. No literal `/home/<user>` anywhere.
2. Add the `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards to
   `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` so a hook-triggered sync cannot nest inside
   `wl sync`'s own temporary worktree, mirroring the sibling implementations.
3. Update the `install_pi.sh` portability warning to reflect the fixed
   behaviour (warning remains a guard for *forked/older* wrappers only).
4. Replace the docs caveat with the actual resolution order and the no-op
   behaviour; document the bypass variables.
5. Add the hermetic regression test described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — replace the hard-coded `exec` with portable resolution + graceful no-op.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — add tmp-worktree and linked-worktree guards; keep `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` bypass.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — adjust the fail-open portability warning/message to the new contract.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — replace the portability caveat with the resolution order and no-op semantics.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` — new hermetic regression tests (worktree add succeeds under a sandboxed `$HOME`; no-op path; bypass; no hard-coded `/home/<user>` in committed hooks).
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — extend only if the installer warning contract changes.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — *Chore: install central wl post-pull hook
  (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing* (completed): installed the
  central symlink and the wrapper-to-central delegation this item now makes
  portable.
- `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` — *SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing
  central script* (closed as duplicate of this item; its reproduction
  transcript, sibling self-contained-hook precedent and `WORKLOG_SKIP_*`
  behaviour are folded in above).
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test
  gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): precedent for project-vs-framework
  hook variants in the same installer block.
- `SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`, `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8` — hook/GIT environment
  investigations that motivate fail-open resolution.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` — pre-push git-identity guard (same hook family; do not
  regress it).
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Related files: `.githooks/pre-push` (v3 pattern for `git rev-parse`-based
  resolution), sibling `.githooks/{post-checkout,worklog-post-pull}` in
  `ContextHub`/`AI_Hell`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** repo-relative resolution is the intended shape (the ACs allow
  either repo-relative delegation or inline logic; the repository already
  commits `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so reusing it is the minimal change).
- **Assumption:** keeping `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as a
  second candidate preserves compatibility with framework projects whose
  wrappers are installed by `install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** `git rev-parse` inside a hook can be misled by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*`
  pollution. Mitigation: `2>/dev/null`, fall back to `dirname "$0"`, then
  `$HOME`, then no-op.
- **Risk:** a no-op can hide a broken install. Mitigation: the stderr line names
  both attempted paths and points at `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** the new test could invoke real `wl` (network/sync side effects).
  Mitigation: sandboxed `$HOME`, stub `wl` on `PATH`, or assert the no-op path
  only; never perform a real sync in the test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting hooks in sibling repositories, redesigning
  `wl sync`, or changing the pre-push gate are out of scope; record as linked
  follow-up items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked in this intake: the seed brief, the
reproduction transcript from the consolidated duplicate, and repository
inspection supplied enough detail to draft an unambiguous brief.

Research performed (evidence links):

- Q (self-resolved): "Does the repository already contain the post-pull
  script?" — Answer: **yes**, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed
  (514 bytes) but unreferenced by the wrappers. Evidence: `rg worklog-post-pull`;
  file contents.
- Q (self-resolved): "Why does the failure not appear on this host?" — Answer:
  the wrappers hard-code `/home/rgardler`, and on this host the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` install (`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP`) provides that exact
  path as a symlink to the repo script, so checkout succeeds and the defect is
  latent. Removing the symlink for one command reproduces `rc=127`; changing
  `$HOME` alone does not, because the path is absolute. Evidence:
  `mv …/worklog-post-pull …; git worktree add …; mv back` (verified during
  intake), `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`.
- Q (self-resolved): "Is there a precedent implementation?" — Answer: **yes**,
  `ContextHub` and `AI_Hell` ship self-contained post-checkout hooks with
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: sibling `.githooks/`
  contents (`ContentCreator` not present on this host).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the defect already tested?" — Answer: **no**.
  `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` tests the installer with synthetic
  hooks; nothing asserts the committed wrappers. Evidence: `rg` over `tests/`.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search "post-pull hook"` / `"worklog hook"`
  found `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` (same defect), closed as a duplicate of this item;
  no other overlapping open or completed item found.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K** – GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, acceptance, acs (+344 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absolute, acceptance, acs, actual (+314 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, actual, add (+294 more)
## Plan (2026-10-27)

**Decision: single leaf item — no child decomposition.** The change is one
atomic fix to a small, tightly-coupled hook contract (three wrappers + the
script they exec + installer wiring + docs) estimated **Small / Medium**
(5.42h expected). Splitting it into child items would leave intermediate
commits with a half-portable hook chain and a red suite — the committed suite
must be green at every commit — so the work is implemented as one vertical
slice that cuts through hooks, installer, tests and docs.

Rationale recorded per the plan skill's step 5 (phasing not required for an
item of this size; documented rather than silently skipped).

**Duplicate check:** `wl search "post-pull hook" | "worklog hook" |
"githooks portability" | "worktree add 127"` found no open item covering these
ACs. `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` is the already-closed duplicate of this item;
`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` (completed) installed the central symlink;
`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (open) is precedent for the *local-then-global
resolution* pattern in the pre-push hook and stays a separate item.

### Implementation order (test-first; suite green at each commit)

1. **Tests first** — add `tests/test_githooks_portability.py`, hermetic and
   offline, covering:
   - (a) static: no committed wrapper contains `/home/<user>` or another
     machine-specific absolute path (guards AC1);
   - (b) temp repository built from the committed `.githooks/` with
     `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed `$HOME` with no `.config/pi`, and
     a stub `wl` on `PATH` → `git worktree add --detach` exits 0, prints no
     `exec: ... not found`, and the repo-relative
     `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the script that ran (marker file);
   - (c) same setup with `worklog-post-pull` removed → `rc=0`, exactly one
     stderr notice naming both attempted locations, stub `wl` never invoked;
   - (d) `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypasses the sync;
   - (e) recursion guards: `PWD` containing `tmp-worktree-`, and a linked
     worktree (`--git-dir` ≠ `--git-common-dir`), both exit before `wl sync`.
2. **Rewrite the three wrappers** (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`,
   `post-rewrite`) to resolve `worklog-post-pull` as: repo-relative
   (`<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"/worklog-post-pull`) → `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/...` →
   one-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. Test for existence/executability before
   `exec` so a missing script can never produce 127. Keep the
   `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` marker (no version bump: `install_pi.sh`
   detects wiring by content, and the sibling projects use v1 markers).
   *Commit A: tests + wrappers.*
3. **Add recursion guards** to `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`: skip
   `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and linked worktrees before the `wl sync` call,
   mirroring the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies; keep the
   `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypass first.
4. **Update `scripts/install_pi.sh`**: the fail-open portability warning must
   now fire only for *legacy/foreign* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution and
   no reference to `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`), and must no
   longer warn about this repository's fixed wrappers; refresh the explanatory
   comment block. *Commit B: guards + installer.*
5. **Docs**: replace the "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph
   in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` with the resolution order, the no-op
   behaviour and the bypass variables. Touch
   `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` only if the installer warning
   contract changed. *Commit C: docs.*
6. **Verify**: changed-scope tests, then the full suite via `/skill:test`
   (AC6); capture AC3 evidence (see below). *Commit D only if fix-ups are
   needed.*

### AC → verification map

| AC | Proven by |
|----|-----------|
| No hard-coded per-user path | static scan (test 1a) + resolution/`exit 0` behaviour in tests 1b/1c |
| Regression test proves `git worktree add` succeeds | tests 1a, 1b, 1c |
| `wl sync` completes its push step without the central install | see *AC3 evidence* note |
| Hooks cannot recurse | test 1e |
| Docs updated | review diff of `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, comment blocks and `install_pi.sh` |
| Full suite passes | `/skill:test` full scope before the dev push |

**AC3 evidence note.** No automated test may perform a real sync (risk noted
below). Preferred proof: a hermetic temp clone with a **local bare remote** and
a sandboxed `$HOME`, running `wl sync` so its push step completes with no
network access and no `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`
workaround. If `wl` cannot push to a local remote in that sandbox, record the
manual transcript (commands + exit codes) as a comment on this item instead —
the AC is satisfied by evidence, not necessarily by a test.

### Implementation notes

- Keep the shared-script model: the wrappers delegate; only
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` contains sync logic (no inlined copies).
- Survive `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution (`SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`,
  `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8`): every `git rev-parse` is `2>/dev/null`-guarded and
  falls through to `$HOME`, then the no-op.
- Do not touch `.githooks/pre-push` / `pre-push.v2`, the full-suite gate or the
  `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker.
- Sibling checkouts (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are reference only; any
  divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item, not an edit here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-27** — Plan applied: single-leaf decision recorded, test-first
  implementation order, AC→verification map and AC3 evidence note added;
  duplicate check performed (no overlapping open item); effort/risk reused from
  the 2026-10-23 estimate (Small / Medium, 5.42h expected); stage advanced to
  `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Plan session (2026-10-27)

No clarifying questions were put to the producer: the intake brief plus the
files verified during this session supplied the plan inputs. Self-resolved
items (each with evidence):

- Q: "Does the repository's committed wrapper content still match the intake
  description?" — **Yes.** Each of `.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge` and
  `post-rewrite` is the 3-comment-line wrapper ending in
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"`; the
  committed `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the shared script and lacks the
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: file contents read
  this session.
- Q: "What exactly do the sibling guards look like, for reuse?" — **Answered**
  by `ContextHub/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and `AI_Hell/.githooks/
  worklog-post-pull`: `case "$PWD" in *tmp-worktree-*) exit 0 ;; esac` then
  `[ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" != "$(git rev-parse
  --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" ] && exit 0`, both before the `wl sync` call.
  Precedent for the *resolution* shape comes from
  `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (local-then-global runner lookup in the v3 pre-push
  hook).
- Q: "How does `install_pi.sh` currently decide to warn?" — **It greps the
  project's `.githooks/post-checkout` for the central path it just installed**
  (`scripts/install_pi.sh`, "Fail-open portability check" block). After this
  change the wrappers no longer name that absolute path first, so the check
  must be rewritten to detect *legacy* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution
  and no `$HOME` candidate) rather than deleted — recorded as step 4.
- Q: "Can the hermetic test really avoid a real sync?" — **Yes, for ACs 2, 4
  and 5**: a stub `wl` on `PATH` records invocation, so no sync runs. AC3
  needs the sync's push step, so the cost/shape is recorded as the *AC3
  evidence* note (local bare remote preferred; transcript otherwise).

OPEN QUESTION (directed to the implementer, not blocking): whether a `wl sync`
push to a **local bare remote** works inside a sandboxed `$HOME` without
credentials. If it does not, the AC3 transcript route applies — no change to
the AC text is needed and the plan is unaffected.

Discovered-from:SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 (during the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS epic).

## Problem

`wl sync` refuses to *merge* worklog commits authored by a sentinel identity
(`t@t.com`) — the quarantine works on the pull side. But nothing stops a
checkout with a stale/sentinel `user.email` from *publishing* worklog commits
under that identity in the first place. That is how the 2026-10-22 incident
happened: the operator's other machine (host `RossGameDev`) synced from a
SorraAgents checkout whose identity was `T <t@t.com>`, and every other clone
then refused to sync until the refs were re-authored by hand.

`scripts/check_git_identity.py` detects this, but it is advisory and only wired
into `.githooks/pre-push` (fail-open: the sync is skipped, the push proceeds) —
`wl sync` invoked directly (as agent sessions do) has no such guard.

## Proposed change (belongs in the worklog CLI, ContextHub repo)

Before pushing worklog data, `wl sync` should refuse when the identity it is
about to commit with is a known sentinel (reuse the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` rule
from `scripts/check_git_identity.py`: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`,
`test@test`, `cache test@test.com`) or empty, with an actionable message and a
`--allow-sentinel-author` escape hatch mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 A `wl sync` (push step) with `user.email` set to a sentinel identity refuses *before* pushing, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`).
- [ ] AC2 The refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or to `syncAllowedAuthors` entries (exact-email rule, no wildcard).
- [ ] AC3 An explicit escape hatch (`--allow-sentinel-author`, audit-logged in the sync output) permits a deliberate one-off, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [ ] AC4 Regression tests cover the sentinel/empty/config-identity decision as a pure function plus one CLI-level refusal test; no network.
- [ ] AC5 Documentation: worklog sync docs describe the pull-side gate and the new push-side guard together.

## Notes

- Until this lands, recurrence prevention is operational: every checkout must have the project identity (`docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` / the identity guard) before its first `wl sync`.
- Cross-repo: the fix lives in the ContextHub worklog CLI; this item tracks it here because the incident surfaced in this project.
data.title: wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (t@t.com)
